checks.note: The excerpt is verbatim. The proposition is faithful. The rationale and limitations match e1 (Feb 2 limited-time Codex access for Free/Go) and e2 (Mar 13–27 doubled off-peak usage, Enterprise excluded). Axis, horizon and unresolved outcome match the reviews. Publishers, dates and relations are correct. The problem is the evidence excerpts: they are cut to fragments that show none of the cited evidence. e1 shows only "Codex", not the limited-time Free/Go availability. e2 shows only "Friday, March 13", without the offer or its March 27 end.

The proposition drops "the very second", which commits the speaker to an immediate reaction. It also softens "endlessly-discounted" and "freaking out". The contract makes a prompt response part of the support condition. The rationale matches e1 (May 2025 adoption, a subgroup result, not significant in the full sample) and e2 (pause on June 15). Outcome, axis and horizon match the reviews. The e1 excerpt "adopt AI" leaves out the subgroup qualifier and the one-year lag, so it misstates the cited finding.
